newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy anti-mafia cops bust big music piracy ring.
newsitem.headline: Italy anti-mafia cops bust big music piracy ring.

text.p: Anti-mafia magistrates have broken up a Naples-based music bootleg organisation in the biggest operation of its kind carried out in Italy, the Federation against Musical Piracy (FPM) said on Tuesday.

After a five-month inquiry, investigating judge Isabella Iaselli ordered 14 Naples residents detained on preliminary charges ranging from criminal association to receiving stolen goods and counterfeiting.

A statement by the Naples public prosecutor's office said the investigation had discovered a major organisation involved in the forgery and fencing, or illegal sell-off, of music cassettes and compact discs.
The probe began when police raided a basement in the southern port city surprising a group of 13 people and seizing thousands of counterfeit cassettes and CDs.

Run by one Naples-based family, the group "operated with ever increasing means and professionality so as to make it the fiercest and most important of organisations involves in musical piracy in Naples," the prosecutor's statement said.
The music industry is seeing an expansion of illegal bootleg copies which account for some 20 percent of the world market for a value of around $2.5 billion a year.
Output of illegal CDs in particular is increasing with production centres mainly in China, Taiwan, Bulgaria and Russia.
